title: Segmentation-driven runtime presets for customer profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated system that computes per-customer and per-route runtime 'presets' (batching and caching configuration candidates) based on observed traffic patterns, assigns a conservative risk score, and supports safe application with canary/dry-run and automated rollback. The presets will be surfaced as recommendations in the Console and exposed via an API for programmatic application. This reduces token/unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and correctness for high-value customers and routes.

Scope:
- Offline recommendation engine that consumes past 30d request traces (sequence length distribution, prefix overlap, QPS, percentiles) and creates candidate presets (batch_size, max_batch_delay_ms, prefix_cache_policy, kv_cache_ttl, quantization_profile).
- Segmentation rules to assign customers and routes to profiles: by customer tier, route tags (e.g., embeddings vs. generation), and explicit allowlist/denylist.
- Risk scoring: model of potential output quality regression (based on prompt pattern change, hallucination risk signals, deterministic test prompts).
- Safe apply flow: dry-run (simulated cost/latency impact), canary rollout (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%), automated rollback triggers (error-rate delta, latency P95 increase, quality regression on eval set).
- Console UI surfaces recommendations, audit trail, and manual override for Dedicated/Private tenants.
- APIs and RBAC: programmatic apply/revert with audit metadata and per-tenant guardrails.

Out of scope for this ticket: quantization algorithm development and low-level kernel selection (handled by runtime team separately).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation generator runs nightly and produces a ranked list of presets for each customer+route pair (or segmentation bucket)
Recommendations contain estimated token savings, expected latency delta, and a risk score with explanation notes
Console shows recommendations with 'Preview impact' dry-run link and an 'Apply with canary' button
Apply flow executes canary rollout to configured percent and monitors guardrail metrics; automatic rollback occurs when thresholds crossed
Audit log entry created for every recommendation and apply/rollback action with user and change diff
API endpoints exist: GET /v1/recommendations?customer=, POST /v1/recommendations/{id}/apply (body: canary_pct, notify_emails)
success_metrics: Aggregate token cost reduction of 6-12% for customers who accepted recommendations within 30d
No more than 0.5% of applied canaries trigger a full rollback due to regression
Mean time to rollback <= 3 minutes from automated trigger
At least 70% of recommended presets get reviewed (accepted or rejected) by PMs/ops within 14 days
implementation_notes: Data inputs: 30d request traces, per-route histograms, customer tier metadata from billing service, prompt evasion indicators from QA evals
Estimator: greedy heuristic first-pass (freq-based prefix cache candidates + batching heuristics), followed by simulated dry-run using recorded traces to estimate cost/latency impact
Risk model: feature set includes prompt pattern drift, fraction of test prompts sensitive to token reduction, past rollback history; initial model is logistic regression to keep explainability
Safe apply: implement canary controller that supports staged percentages and pluggable rollback rules (error-rate, latency_p95, eval_score_diff), with Prometheus alerts and Console notifications
Segmentation: default buckets = {free, standard, enterprise, internal-exempt}; support custom allowlists/denylists at customer and route level
RBAC: only users with 'ops:apply-presets' can trigger full rollouts; canary apply allowed for 'ops:trial'
Telemetry: emit recommendation_id, preset_hash, canary_pct, metric_snapshots to cost/observability team dashboard (Grafana link below)
